results.proposedAnswer: Datumwise holds that a request is servable when both conditions are met: (1) it is analytically established — the requested analytical object exists under the governed analytical model and the requested derivation is lawful — and (2) support is sufficient — the evidence and required state for this request are presently available [S1]. Servability is determined per request under current grounds; computability or dataset/model availability alone does not make a request servable [S1]. Examples from the framework: a missing feed can leave a lawful request unsupported; an unlawful reduction can leave abundant data unable to establish the result; an unresolved population can make a computable denominator analytically unestablished [S1]. Servability grants analytical permission to answer; whether the answer is actually served then depends on authorization, risk, and disclosure conditions [S1].
